question.text: A spherical bubble inside water has radius <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>R</mi></math>. Take the pressure inside the bubble and the water pressure to be <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>p</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>.</mo></math> The bubble now gets compressed radially in an adiabatic manner so that its radius becomes <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>(</mo><mi>R</mi><mo>-</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>)</mo></math>. For <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>a</mi><mo>≪</mo><mi>R</mi></math> the magnitude of the work done in the process is given by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mrow><mn>4</mn><mi>π</mi><msub><mi>P</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mi>R</mi><msup><mi>a</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mfenced><mi>X</mi><mo>,</mo></math> where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>X</mi></math> is a constant and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>γ</mi><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>C</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo>/</mo><msub><mi>C</mi><mi>V</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>41</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>30</mn></math>. The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>X</mi></math> is______
